title: COLLATION behaves differently if set on CREATE TABLE vs ALTER TABLE

comments.text:
Description:
Sorting behaves differently when the COLLATE setting for a table is set on CREATE TABLE DDL or via ALTER TABLE post creation of a table.

Example: 

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bad ( col varchar(512) ) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS good ( col varchar(512) );
ALTER TABLE good CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;

Sorting by column `col` will behave differently in the `good` vs `bad` table.

How to repeat:
https://gist.github.com/joaomneto/c27c6fb98c0a741e3e59be0aae23a3b5

Create both tables:

```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bad ( col varchar(512) ) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS good ( col varchar(512) );
ALTER TABLE good CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;
```

Insert test data:

```
INSERT INTO good (col) VALUES ('tag_1'), ('tag_4'), ('tag.x');
INSERT INTO bad (col) VALUES ('tag_1'), ('tag_4'), ('tag.x');
```

Select data sorted by column `col`

```
SELECT col FROM good GROUP BY col ORDER BY col DESC;
SELECT col FROM bad GROUP BY col ORDER BY col DESC;
```

First select on the good table will produce:

```
tag.x
tag_4
tag_1
```

Second select on the bad table will produce:

```
tag_4
tag_1
tag.x
```
This behaviour does not occur in MySQL 5.7.

Hello Joao Neto,

Thank you for the report and feedback.

regards,
Umesh

Posted by developer:
 
Not a bug. In 5.7 those table would be equal, but in 8.0 and later they will not.

mysql> show create table bad\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
       Table: bad
Create Table: CREATE TABLE `bad` (
  `col` varchar(512) COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_general_ci
1 row in set (0,01 sec)

mysql> show create table good\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
       Table: good
Create Table: CREATE TABLE `good` (
  `col` varchar(512) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_general_ci
1 row in set (0,00 sec)

the reason is that utfmb4 has a different deafult collation in 8.0 and later than in 5.7, and in the two collations, '_' and '.' collates differently:

mysql> select '.' > '_' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
+--------------------------------------+
| '.' > '_' collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci |
+--------------------------------------+
|                                    1 |
+--------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)

mysql> select '.' > '_' collate utf8mb4_general_ci;
+--------------------------------------+
| '.' > '_' collate utf8mb4_general_ci |
+--------------------------------------+
|                                    0 |
+--------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)

(Note that in the given example '.' is used before 'x' in the string 'tag.x').

Posted by developer:
 
This is expected behavior. utf8mb4 has different default collations in 5.7 vs 8.0 and later. See detailed explanation in previous comment.

I understand that there is a different default collation. But I am forcing the collation to utf8mb4_general_ci, and I should be able to do that both via create or alter table. But when doing via create table I get a different sorting behaviour than if I do it via an alter table.
Sorry, I read your comment more attentively. Why on the bad table does the column have a different collation than what is set on the table?
Sorry, I mean on the `good` table
Oh. I understand now. Thank you.
